title: Why Did the Nations Join to Slay
description: Why Did the Nations Join to Slay in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 2, part 2, headed “The same”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Why did the na-tions join to slay The Lord's a-noint-ed Son? Why did they cast his laws a-way, And tread his gos-pel down?

lines: Why did the nations join to slay
Why did they cast his laws away,
The Lord that sits above the skies,
He speaks with vengeance in his eyes,
"I make my holy hill his throne,
"Ask me, my Son, and then enjoy
Be wise, ye rulers of the earth,
Adore the king of heavenly birth,
With humble love address his throne,
For if he frown ye die;
Those are secure, and those alone,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
